text.p: Italian bonds and futures were knocked back at the close on selling pressure after a buoyant session on domestic political jitters over judicial problems of Prime Minister Romano Prodi and some retracement in Treasuries and Bunds, traders said.

Prodi today denied an allegation of conflict of interest forming part of a magistrate's request to send him for trial over alleged irregularities when he headed state holding IRI in 1993. But Milan traders said the market slipped on extracts of an interview with PDS leader Massimo D'Alema to a weekly where he said if Prodi fell there would have to be new elections.

London traders said they were not aware of the D'Alema interview and put down the late slide in Btps to a retracement in Treasuries and Bunds. "There's long liquidation out there," one said. Bunds had earlier hit new highs in cash and futures.
"There are no major reasons to sell but those wanting to take profits are just grabbing any opportunity which comes up," one Milan primary dealer said.

At today's end-month Treasury auction of 36.5 trillion lire worth of short term bills (Bots) yields continued to fall, especially on 12-months Bots, where the gross yield fell to 6.63 percent from 6.97 percent two weeks ago.
